The PR body's measurements were read as input, not as conclusions; every count below is this review's own measurement. No environment variable value is printed anywhere in this record.

### ① Derived judgments

1. File surface. One commit (608b9084, author Claude, PR author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, head repo = base repo, draft, base `main`, trailers `Co-Authored-By: Claude` + `Claude-Session:`, no model identifier; `check-commit-card-trailers` exit 0 on the range). `git diff --numstat 0a4e74ea 608b9084`, the REST file listing and the PR body agree on exactly one path, `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs` +35/−156 (blob f483372c → 1f6d84fe). The claim's file surface (6589842500) was this file plus any skill or reference line naming H24 or H25 as a live row; no skill or reference line names either (measured in 4 below), so the second half is empty. Correct, and on surface.
2. H25 is gone as a row, whole. Removed on the head: the header-docblock entry (15 lines), the rationale block (40 lines), `AWAITING_MAINTAINER_CONFLICT_REASON` (10 lines, read only by H25 at the merge-base, measured by grep), `export function h25AwaitingMaintainerExclusivity` (18 lines), `H25: 'state'` in `HALF_STATE_FAMILY_BAND` (62 → 61 keys, measured by import), the two sweep-loop lines `const doubleState = …` / `findings.push([issue, 'H25', …])`, and the `h25row` test helper. `git grep -E 'H25|h25|AWAITING_MAINTAINER_CONFLICT_REASON'` over the head file returns nothing; `head.h25AwaitingMaintainerExclusivity` is `undefined` on import. Nothing outside the file imported the predicate or the map at the merge-base. Correct.
3. H29 takes over exactly H25's pairs. The one behaviour line removed is `if (a === AWAITING_MAINTAINER_LABEL || b === AWAITING_MAINTAINER_LABEL) continue; // H25's`; the H3 exclusion (`pmStatePairKey(a, b) === H3_PAIR_KEY`) stays. Measured by importing both trees and judging every non-empty subset of the six-label vocabulary (`PM_EXCLUSIVE_STATE_LABELS` identical on both trees: awaiting, queue, dispatched, blocked, on-hold, needs-user-decision) as an open card: 63 sets; H25 fired on 31 (every set containing the awaiting label and at least one other state); the head's H29 fires on all 31, 0 misses; on every one of the 31 sets the head's H29 sentence names, in backticks, every non-awaiting state present; whether any of H3/H25/H29 fires is unchanged on all 63 sets; H3 is unchanged on all 63; on the 31 sets without the awaiting label the head's H29 return is byte-identical to the merge-base's (`null` or the same sentence). Edge cards: awaiting alone → `null`; awaiting + `pm:blocking` + `domain:skills` → `null` (non-state labels still excluded); closed awaiting + queue → `null` (closed cards stay H22's); `undefined` → `null` on both trees. On the triple awaiting + queue + dispatched the head's H29 names awaiting+queue and awaiting+dispatched and still skips queue+dispatched, which H3 reports: one breach, one row, as the H29 header requires. Correct; the PR body's three numbers (63, 31/31, byte-identical off the awaiting label) reproduce.
4. H24 and its readers untouched. `h24QueuedWithAssignee`'s body is byte-identical on both trees (same md5 of the function span); over 126 probe cards (63 subsets × assigned/unassigned) its return is identical on both trees; its sweep-loop call and `'H24'` push stay; the five `H24:` self-test cases and the H8 case `…and points at H24 as the state it prevents` (head line 30547) are not in the diff. The only lines mentioning H24 that changed are three comment lines that also named H25 (the `## H24 + H25` docblock heading, the `GOVERNED_PR_DECISION_LABEL` note, the sweep-loop comment). H24's one reader outside the file, `scripts/ci/scheduled-full-run.mjs:536`, is not in the diff. Correct, per ruling point 2 and 3.
5. No remaining live reference to H25 anywhere in the tree except one comment. `git grep -I -E '\bH25\b'` over the whole head tree (and over the merge-base) returns exactly one line: `scripts/pm/ensure-pm-labels.sh:212`, a shell comment that lists the label's "named consumers" as `H25 (that exclusivity), H11, H13's PM_STATE_LABELS and H22's PM_RESIDUE_LABELS`. Nothing under `.claude/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/**`, `.github/**` or any other script names H25 as a row; `state-machine.md:8` already names H29/H30 as the authority for the six-state ONE-OF, which this PR makes true for the awaiting pairs as well. Judged in ③ and ④: a one-word stale comment outside the surface, no behaviour, correctly recorded in the PR body as a follow-up.
6. The self-test count and its decomposition. Head 5202, merge-base 5219, difference 17. From the diff: 18 `t(` lines removed, of which 2 are per-label loops over the 5-member `AWAITING_MAINTAINER_EXCLUSIVE_LABELS` (16 + 10 = 26 cases); 5 `t(` lines added, of which 1 is a loop (4 + 5 = 9 cases); 26 − 9 = 17. By group: 14 H25 cases (9 singles + the 5-case loop) removed with no replacement; `H29: …and H25 does fire on it` removed with no replacement; the two H55 adjacency cases (H25 silent, H29 silent) replaced by one (H29 silent): net −1; `H55 reconciliation: H25's deferral points at this row` removed (it asserted H25's header prose, which the ruling says goes): net −1. The seven flipped cases are the single `H29: a pair containing the awaiting state is this row's` (was `…is H25's`, `null` → `'string'`), the 5-case loop `H29: awaiting + <state> fires here` (was `stays H25's row`, `null` → `'string'`) and `H29: …and names the awaiting pairs too` (was `…does not re-report`, `false` → `true`); the remaining added line is a rename of the `awaitingPlusTwo` case with the same assertion. One `b(` line changed in BATTERY66 (name only, `H25's pair` → `H29's pair`, same assertion). Correct, and the PR body's breakdown matches.
7. No battery shrank, no pin moved. The battery roster printed by both self-tests is identical in order and in every n/floor: H66 182/172, H19 37/34 and 26/16, H65 46/42, H67 158/158, H2/H47/H66 213/184, ISSUE_BODY_LIMIT 55/52, H19/H26 11/10, H68 26/24, H9 10/9, lane aliases 25/22, yielded claim 21/19, H69 70/40, H43 89/80, H70/H71 31/30, H72 22/20, H73 28/25. No `b(` case was removed. Correct.
8. What stays, per ruling point 3. `AWAITING_MAINTAINER_EXCLUSIVE_LABELS` is still exported with its five members (measured by import) and `PM_EXCLUSIVE_STATE_LABELS` still spreads it; the `queued` fixture is still defined at head line 30491 and used by the H3, H8, H19, H22, H24 and H29 cases; `SEEN_LABEL_PAGES` is unchanged and lists `AWAITING_MAINTAINER_LABEL`, so every card H25 could have seen is still listed into the same `seen` loop where H29 runs (head lines 23268 → 23314). The live coverage therefore moves with the predicate, not only the predicate. Correct.
9. Comment and name re-pointing. The `AWAITING_MAINTAINER_LABEL` reader list, the `GOVERNED_PR_DECISION_LABEL` note, H55's header (two places), the H66/H67 population notes, the patrol input-set note, the sweep-loop comment and the BATTERY66 case name now say H29 where they said H25 or H25/H29. The H29 header's "both exclusions … in both directions" paragraph was rewritten to the one exclusion that remains; the `PM_STATE_CLAIM` note about why it is "NOT merged with H25's map" is removed with the map. Correct, and no output string changed by these edits.
10. Gates. `check-governed-merges.mjs --branch HEAD`: 0 of 1 path hit the register, NOT governed, 191 changed lines, exit 0; the claim and the PR body say the same. Of the 47 derived commands, 38 exit 0 here and reproduce the dev's "all 47 exit 0" for the subset this container can run (the file's own gates among them: `check:pm-half-states` 5202 cases, `check:scripts-symbol-anchors` 0 dangling anchors after the deletion, `check:self-test-wired` with the `check:pm-half-states` alias still paired to its lint.yml step); the other 9 stop on this container's missing `yaml`, `typescript`, `@typescript-eslint/parser` or `@changesets/cli` dependency (PREREQUISITE NOT MET exit 3, or `Cannot find package` exit 1 in `check-self-test-workflow-commands`), not on the diff, and are read from CI instead: `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests` and `Lint & Repo Gates` are all `success` on the head. `check:pm-half-states` is the alias CI runs for this file (lint.yml line 1265, in `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, success on the head). The `half-state-patrol.yml` pull_request trigger fires on this path and runs the live sweep with the head's code (anchor write skipped, body to the step summary); its conclusion is read in the Check-runs line.
11. PR body against the head. First content line `Part of #29471`, zero verbs beside the card number; the body's only issue number is 29471 (four mentions, none within a closing keyword's reach; a case-insensitive scan for close/fix/resolve forms before `#<n>` returns nothing); `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are present as their own lines and right (no published package, no spec, no governed text); `PR-body guards` check success. The body's numbers (5202/5219, 17, seven flipped, 63/31/31, +35/−156, 47 commands, exit 0 for governed-merges and trailers) all reproduce. The acceptance note on `ensure-pm-labels.sh:212` is accurate. No model identifier in body, title or commit. Correct.
12. Nothing new on any surface: no gate, no row, no constant, no label, no workflow, no package. The card asked for deletion "with their self-test cases; no behaviour change in the rows that stay"; the ruling (6589866189 point 1) explicitly accepts the one staying-row change as the merge of two detectors of one state, and 3 above measures that no state loses its report. Correct.

### ② Semver level

None. No published package, no `packages/spec/src/**`, no TypeScript; a `scripts/pm` tool's self-test and predicate. `skip-changeset` is the right declaration and Check Changeset is `success` on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev `open_questions`: none; the R1 report is the PR body (no separate os-dev-report on the card for R1). The census's two open questions (6586191438) were about tier 2 and the sweep as a whole and do not bear on this PR.
- The ruling's narrowing (R1 → H25 only, H24 stays) is implemented as ruled: H24 untouched, the H8 case naming H24 untouched, the H55 header-prose case removed, `AWAITING_MAINTAINER_EXCLUSIVE_LABELS` and `queued` kept. No flag.
- `scripts/pm/ensure-pm-labels.sh:212`: a shell comment still names H25 as the label's exclusivity consumer. It is outside the claim's file surface (a script, not a skill or reference line), it is comment text with no behaviour and no gate reads it, and review-checklist's four conditions for an in-place out-of-surface fix (same defect class, mechanical, unclaimed, same gate family, with the claim's file surface revised in the same round) were not exercised; the dev declared it instead. Judged a follow-up, not a should-fix for this PR: the correct spelling now is "H29 (that exclusivity)", one word, and it belongs to whichever family next touches that file (or a one-line patch after this lands). Recorded here so the tier-2 wave inherits it.
- H29's sentence for an awaiting pair now carries each label's own `PM_STATE_CLAIM` clause instead of H25's per-pairing "specific lie" clause. The remedy (keep the one true state, drop the rest in a single write) is the same, both labels are still named in backticks, and the ruling accepted the merge; noted, not flagged.
- Independence: PR author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, commit author Claude, commit `Claude-Session:` is the dev session (`session_01J8VVAmM3BRQQcQSA67VE3L`), not the reviewer's; no off-relay author note is owed. The PR thread carries the seat's `Contract-review-claim:` for this head (6590192434) and no other record.
- Not governed, Tier S path: landing by the ordinary queue once the check-runs are all green.

### ④ Design judgment

Per hits file, against the card's scenario (a row with no named reader and no 30-day citation costs a self-test and a live pass on every patrol run; the discipline text gives such an instrument deletion as its only in-flight work) and the ruling's constraint (no state loses its report):

- `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs`, H25's removal: cut whole rather than trimmed. The rationale block, the conflict-reason map and the predicate existed only for each other, and the map's prose about "the second half of one sentence" was the reason it was never merged into `PM_STATE_CLAIM`; with the row gone there is no second half to keep. Leaving the header entry or the band row would leave a registry naming a row the loop never pushes, which the registry-coverage pin would then be asserting for nothing. Holds.
- H29's awaiting skip: the right line to delete, and the only one. At the merge-base H29 already owned the general ONE-OF invariant and the vocabulary constant H25 contributed to (`PM_EXCLUSIVE_STATE_LABELS` spreads `AWAITING_MAINTAINER_EXCLUSIVE_LABELS`), so the skip was the one place the two rows met; removing it makes H29 the single owner of 14 of the 15 pairs and H3 of the fifteenth, which is what `state-machine.md:8` already said H29 was. Keeping the H3 exclusion is correct because H3 keeps its own measured specimen and sentence. The self-test's seven flipped cases pin the new ownership in the same two-direction form the header demands. Holds.
- The H55 reconciliation case that read H25's header prose through `readFileSync(SELF_PATH)`: it asserted a sentence that no longer exists and could not have been kept without keeping prose about a deleted row; removing it with the row is the ruling's point 3. The remaining H55 reconciliation cases still read the file for the ager's two notes, which are untouched. Holds.
- H24 kept and its one reader (`scheduled-full-run.mjs:536`) untouched: the census's grouping of H24 with H25 was wrong on the merits (an assignee intersection, not a label pair), the dev measured that before deleting and the seat ruled on it; the PR does what the ruling says and records H24's tier-2 standing in the body rather than in code. Holds.
